data.content:
Here are the benchmark results comparing .NET 9 vs .NET 10:

## Benchmark Results — TextAnalyzer (1000 words)

| Method | .NET 9 | .NET 10 | Change | Allocated |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **AverageWordLength** | 5.53 μs | 1.36 μs | **~4x faster** ✅ | 0 B (both) |
| **WordLengthHistogram** | 9.46 μs | 3.32 μs | **~2.8x faster** ✅ | 104 B (both) |
| **UniqueWordCount** | 22.12 μs | 32.20 μs | **~46% slower** ⚠️ | 1552 B (both) |

**Summary:**
- `AverageWordLength` and `WordLengthHistogram` see significant performance gains on .NET 10 (likely due to loop/iteration optimizations in RyuJIT).
- `UniqueWordCount` regressed ~46% — this may warrant investigation into `HashSet<string>` behavior changes in .NET 10.
- Memory allocations are identical across both runtimes.

> **Note:** This machine may have been under load; the .NET 9 `AverageWordLength` result had high variance (StdDev 1.56 μs). The .NET 10 runs were more stable.
